entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to tonify Qi, reinforce the exterior body defense (Wei Qi), and support overall vitality and immune endurance.
entries.typical_preparation: Simmered into warm herbal tea infusions, broths, or slow-cooked wellness soups.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Caution advised during acute colds, fever, or active infections with high heat. May interact with immunosuppressant medications or blood pressure treatments. Consult a qualified practitioner before regular use.
entries.source_note: Shennong Bencao Jing (Divine Farmer's Materia Medica) / Pharmacopoeia of the PRC

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to deeply invigorate primordial Qi, nourish spleen and lung energy, calm the mind, and promote mental clarity.
entries.typical_preparation: Gently simmered as an herbal tea infusion or incorporated into double-boiled tonic soups.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Not recommended for individuals with severe hypertension, active heat conditions, or high fever. Avoid taking with strong tea or radish. May interact with blood thinners and diabetes medications.
entries.source_note: Shennong Bencao Jing (Divine Farmer's Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to nourish Liver and Kidney Yin, brighten the eyes, and support healthy aging and vitality.
entries.typical_preparation: Steeped in warm herbal tea infusions, added to oatmeal or soups, or consumed as a dietary snack.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Use with caution if experiencing acute diarrhea, spleen weakness with heavy dampness, or active fever. May interact with anticoagulant medications such as warfarin.
entries.source_note: Bencao Gangmu (Compendium of Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to clear internal heat, soothe the liver, relieve eye fatigue, and calm mild headaches.
entries.typical_preparation: Steeped in hot water as a refreshing herbal tea, often combined with Goji berries.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Caution for individuals with severe Yang deficiency or cold spleen/stomach prone to diarrhea. Avoid if allergic to ragweed or plants in the Asteraceae family.
entries.source_note: Shennong Bencao Jing (Divine Farmer's Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to warm the middle burner, dispel cold, ease mild stomach discomfort, and alleviate nausea.
entries.typical_preparation: Sliced and steeped in boiling water as a warm tea or added as a culinary spice in soups and stews.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Avoid excessive consumption in conditions of internal heat, Yin deficiency with dry throat, or stomach ulcers. May increase risk of bleeding if taken with high-dose blood thinners.
entries.source_note: Mingyi Bielu (Records of Famous Physicians)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to warm the meridians, disperse coldness, support cardiovascular circulation, and warm kidney Yang.
entries.typical_preparation: Simmered as an ingredient in warm herbal tea blends or culinary spices.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Contraindicated during pregnancy and in conditions of internal heat or bleeding disorders. May interact with blood pressure and blood sugar lowering drugs.
entries.source_note: Shennong Bencao Jing (Divine Farmer's Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to harmonize other herbal ingredients, tonify Spleen Qi, soothe the throat, and ease mild muscle tension.
entries.typical_preparation: Simmered into tea blends or decoctions as a balancing component.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Long-term or excessive use is not recommended for individuals with high blood pressure, fluid retention, or kidney disease. May interact with diuretics, corticosteroids, and blood pressure medications.
entries.source_note: Shennong Bencao Jing (Divine Farmer's Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM as a premier Blood-tonifying herb to nourish Blood, invigorate circulation, and regulate menstrual cycles.
entries.typical_preparation: Slowly cooked in herbal soup bases or steeped in warm decoctions.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Avoid during heavy menstrual bleeding, acute diarrhea, or pregnancy unless specifically directed by a healthcare provider. May interact with anticoagulant and antiplatelet drugs.
entries.source_note: Shennong Bencao Jing (Divine Farmer's Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to drain dampness, support Spleen function, promote fluid balance, and calm the spirit.
entries.typical_preparation: Cooked in rice porridge (congee), herbal decoctions, or steeped in wellness teas.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Use with caution in conditions of excessive urination or severe fluid depletion. Generally very mild and well-tolerated.
entries.source_note: Shennong Bencao Jing (Divine Farmer's Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to regulate Qi, strengthen the Spleen, dry dampness, and dissolve phlegm in chest and stomach.
entries.typical_preparation: Steeped in hot water as a digestive tea or added to slow-cooked soups and stews.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Use with caution in conditions of dry cough from Yin deficiency or internal heat with blood coughing. Avoid excessive use in hot climates.
entries.source_note: Shennong Bencao Jing (Divine Farmer's Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to moisten the Lungs, clear heart heat, soothe dry coughs, and promote tranquil sleep.
entries.typical_preparation: Slowly cooked in sweet dessert soups, porridges, or warm herbal infusions.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Caution for individuals with cold-type diarrhea or severe Spleen Yang deficiency. Generally mild and nutritious.
entries.source_note: Shennong Bencao Jing (Divine Farmer's Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to nourish Lung and Stomach Yin, enhance skin hydration, and generate body fluids.
entries.typical_preparation: Stewed gently into a gelatinous sweet dessert soup with red dates or pears.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Avoid during early stages of acute colds or cough with profuse phlegm. Highly suitable for general dietary hydration.
entries.source_note: Bencao Gangmu (Compendium of Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to tonify Spleen and Stomach Qi, nourish Blood, and moderate harsh properties of other herbs.
entries.typical_preparation: Simmered into warm herbal teas, rice porridges, or daily soups.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Avoid excessive intake if experiencing dental caries, severe abdominal distension from damp-heat, or intestinal parasites.
entries.source_note: Shennong Bencao Jing (Divine Farmer's Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to transform food stagnation (especially from meat and fats), invigorate Blood circulation, and support digestion.
entries.typical_preparation: Steeped as a tangy warm tea infusion or prepared as a fruit preserve.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Caution for individuals with severe stomach hyperacidity or gastric ulcers. Avoid during pregnancy due to potential uterine stimulation.
entries.source_note: Xinxiu Bencao (Newly Revised Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in TCM to clear summer heat, detoxify the body, and drain internal damp-heat.
entries.typical_preparation: Boiled into a cooling summer soup or tea beverage.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Not suitable for cold Yang-deficient constitutions prone to cold limbs and diarrhea. May reduce the potency of certain warm herbal medicines when consumed simultaneously.
entries.source_note: Bencao Gangmu (Compendium of Materia Medica)

entries.traditional_uses: Classic TCM formula traditionally used as the foundational baseline to tonify Spleen and Stomach Qi, relieve fatigue, and support digestive assimilation.
entries.typical_preparation: Prepared as a warm decoction or slow-simmered herbal soup blend containing Ginseng/Codonopsis, Atractylodes, Poria, and Licorice.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Not recommended during high fever, acute heat illnesses, or severe fluid dryness. Professional evaluation recommended prior to use.
entries.source_note: Taiping Huimin Heji Jufang (Formularies of the Bureau of People's Welfare Pharmacy)

entries.traditional_uses: Classic TCM formula traditionally used to nourish Kidney and Liver Yin, relieving dry mouth, low back weakness, and warm palm sensations.
entries.typical_preparation: Traditionally taken as water-honey pills or warm decoctions.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Contraindicated for individuals with weak Spleen digestion, severe abdominal bloating, or acute diarrhea. Consult a certified practitioner for proper evaluation.
entries.source_note: Xiao'er Yaozheng Zhizhi (Key to Therapeutics of Children's Diseases)

entries.traditional_uses: Classic TCM formula traditionally used to soothe Liver Qi stagnation, nourish Blood, strengthen the Spleen, and relieve mood tension or stress.
entries.typical_preparation: Prepared as a warm tea infusion or herbal decoction incorporating Bupleurum, Angelica, Peony, Atractylodes, and Mint.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Caution during pregnancy or heavy menstrual bleeding. Professional consultation recommended to ensure pattern match.
entries.source_note: Taiping Huimin Heji Jufang (Formularies of the Bureau of People's Welfare Pharmacy)

entries.traditional_uses: Classic TCM formula traditionally used to solidify the exterior, stop spontaneous sweating, and strengthen protective Wei Qi against seasonal cold exposure.
entries.typical_preparation: Steeped as a warm herbal tea infusion composed of Astragalus, Atractylodes, and Saposhnikovia (Fangfeng).
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Not intended for use during high fever or acute heat-type respiratory infections. Consult a practitioner for seasonal guidance.
entries.source_note: Danxi Xinfa (Danxi's Mastery of Medicine)

entries.traditional_uses: Classic TCM formula traditionally used to dry dampness, transform phlegm, regulate Qi, and harmonize the stomach.
entries.typical_preparation: Simmered into a warm herbal tea infusion featuring Aged Tangerine Peel (Chenpi), Pinellia (Banxia), Poria, and Licorice.
entries.cautions_and_contraindications: Contraindicated in dry cough caused by Yin deficiency or blood depletion. Professional diagnostic guidance recommended.
entries.source_note: Taiping Huimin Heji Jufang (Formularies of the Bureau of People's Welfare Pharmacy)
